_comment: Template for state/profile.json. Copy this file to ../state/profile.json during first-run enrollment (see SKILL.md) and fill it in. This is the one shared identity/org-chart file the whole acos family (cos, acos-email-sort, acos-jira-analysis, acos-calendar-analysis, and future acos skills) reads from — keep it here, not duplicated per skill.

staff._comment: LEGACY field, not read by acos-calendar-analysis — other acos skills (e.g. acos-email-sort) already read this as 'my core team' for their own purposes. Kept as-is; use `reports`/`team` below for acos-calendar-analysis. `is_executive_assistant: true` on exactly one entry is how acos-email-sort resolves `ea_name`/`ea_email` — a deliberate explicit flag rather than matching on `role` text, since role phrasing varies too much to match reliably.

reports._comment: STRICT management-chain fact: everyone who reports to the owner, directly or through someone who reports to them, flattened regardless of depth — an org-chart fact, not a judgment call. Feeds exactly three things in acos-calendar-analysis: (1) the People-leadership category's 2-person-1:1 rule — exactly one other attendee AND they're on this list; (2) the People-leadership category's management-keyword rule, jointly with `team` below; (3) the Audience tag's 'direct team' value — ALL non-organizer attendees are on this list (see calendar_analysis._audience_tag_comment for the full priority order).

team._comment: LOOSER 'who I consider my team day-to-day' fact — a superset of `reports` that can also include people who don't formally report to the owner (e.g. a dotted-line collaborator). Feeds three things: (1) the People-leadership category's management-keyword rule, jointly with `reports` above; (2) the Operating-rhythm category default — an internal multi-person meeting where every attendee is the owner plus people on Team/Reports, with no Shepherd present; (3) the Audience tag's 'broader internal' value — ALL non-organizer attendees are on Team but not narrowly all on Reports (see calendar_analysis._audience_tag_comment).

vip_senders._comment: This is also the 'Shepherd' group referenced by acos-calendar-analysis's Strategy-and-transformation audience default — do not create a separate list for that.

partner_vendors._comment: functional_area powers acos-calendar-analysis's Functional Area tag and the Stakeholder-vs-External distinction. One of: Finance, HR, Legal, Compliance, Revenue, Engineering, Operations, Security, Data — or null if it doesn't fit any.

functional_areas._comment: Flat per-area directories used for acos-calendar-analysis's Functional Area tag. Match by email only, never by name. A person may appear in more than one area. Any area may be an empty list. `Systems` is literal product/tool ownership (HubSpot, CRM, Give Interactive, Jira, TalentLMS, Rippling, etc.) — distinct from `Engineering`, which is dev/infra work.

protected_senders.name: Example Contact
protected_senders.reason: ongoing personal/business relationship — never auto-decline or auto-file without a human look

jira_workspaces._shared_defaults_note: Org-wide values (the Jira site and its Product Discovery field IDs, the Functional Area tagging vocabulary, the time-allocation benchmark tables, the default working hours) live in acos-aboutme's shipped references/defaults.json, not here. Consuming skills load that first and overlay this file, so anything set here wins and anything omitted falls back to the shared default. Set a key here only to deliberately differ.
jira_workspaces._comment: Workspace groups for acos-jira-analysis (and future acos skills). Each group is a list of one or more Jira project keys — don't assume one project per group. Only the project keys are personal — cloud_id, upcoming_window_days and the Product Discovery field IDs come from the shared defaults file; set them here only to differ from the org.

calendar_analysis._shared_defaults_note: Org-wide values (the Jira site and its Product Discovery field IDs, the Functional Area tagging vocabulary, the time-allocation benchmark tables, the default working hours) live in acos-aboutme's shipped references/defaults.json, not here. Consuming skills load that first and overlay this file, so anything set here wins and anything omitted falls back to the shared default. Set a key here only to deliberately differ.
calendar_analysis._comment: Config specific to acos-calendar-analysis, grouped the same way jira_workspaces groups acos-jira-analysis's config. known_meeting_series is the one sub-key acos-calendar-analysis writes back to directly (sticky corrections) — every other field in this whole profile stays read-only to consuming skills.
calendar_analysis._audience_tag_comment: The Audience tag (direct team / broader internal / peer / Shepherd-executive / board / existing partner / prospective external) is evaluated in this exact priority order, first match wins, over the event's non-organizer attendees: (1) board — any attendee is on vip_senders with a title containing 'Board'; (2) Shepherd/executive — any attendee is on vip_senders otherwise (presence alone counts, same as the Strategy-and-transformation default); (3) existing partner — any external attendee AND every external domain present is a partner_vendors domain; (4) prospective external — any external attendee, not all partner domains; (5) direct team — ALL non-organizer attendees are on `reports`; (6) broader internal — ALL non-organizer attendees are on `team`; (7) peer — internal, none of the above. Board/Shepherd are deliberately 'any attendee' checks (one exec in a big room still changes the read); direct-team/broader-internal are deliberately 'all attendees' checks (they describe the room's overall makeup, not one match in a crowd).
calendar_analysis._ignored_addresses_comment: Personal/family addresses that show up as attendees on a company-wide culture event (a staff member's spouse cc'd on a devotional or celebration call) but aren't a real external attendee or business relationship -- filtered out at the earliest point so category classification, the Audience tag, the Functional Area tag, and prep-flag attendee/external counts all treat these as if they were never on the invite.

known_meeting_series._comment: The primary mechanism for classifying recurring meetings consistently. match_patterns are lowercase substrings checked against the event subject (case-insensitive) — list more than one to support simple aliases. category is one of the seven primary categories. tags is optional and may pre-set any of the Step 4 tags. Corrections on a recurring series write back here automatically.

time_allocation_target_overrides._comment: Optional personal override, tighter or looser than the position-type default, keyed by category name to a [min, max] pair. Empty unless the person explicitly asks for a personal target. Never force this to be filled in.
